text:
alice: Quick share — ran the cross-device kernel autotune pass this morning comparing L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100. High level: kernel choices and seq-len paths matter a lot for p99 on shorter requests.

ben: Nice. TL;DR numbers? :eyes:

alice: TL;DR — with the same model/config (gpt-like, 1.2B weights, fp16):
- A100 (single): ~420 tokens/s @ seq=512, batch=4 (p50 ~38ms, p99 ~105ms)
- H100 (single): ~470 tokens/s @ seq=512, batch=4 (p50 ~35ms, p99 ~95ms)
- A10 (single): ~230 tokens/s @ seq=512, batch=4 (p50 ~70ms, p99 ~210ms)
- L4/T4 (single): ~160-190 tokens/s @ seq=512, batch=4 (p50 ~95ms, p99 ~300ms)

carla: Woah those p99 deltas are big. Were you using the same kernel family everywhere?

alice: No — autotuner picked different kernels by arch. On A100/H100 we favor large-tile tensor-core matmul kernels plus fused rotary+attn kernels; on A10/L4/T4 it picked smaller-block matmuls and slower attention kernels with explicit shared-mem reductions.

dmitri: Did you try sequence-length-dependent routing? For short chat seqs we sometimes get better perf by switching to a low-latency kernel path earlier.

alice: Yep — added a simple seq threshold switch in the runtime: seq<=128 -> low-latency path (smaller KV-cache footprint, narrow matmul kernel), seq>128 -> throughput path (larger tiles, more batching). That cut p99 on A10 by ~30% for chat-like loads.

ben: Can you paste the autotune presets you used? Want to baseline on Dedicated clusters.

alice: Paste below — it's the minimal preset bundle we used (applied per-device profile):
```json
{
  "presets": {
    "a100_h100": {
      "kernel_family": "tensor_core_large_tile",
      "tile_size": 256,
      "attention_impl": "fused_rope_attn",
      "seq_switch": 128,
      "kv_cache_layout": "packed",
      "prefer_fp16_math": true
    },
    "a10_l4_t4": {
      "kernel_family": "small_block_mm",
      "tile_size": 64,
      "attention_impl": "split_sharedmem_attn",
      "seq_switch": 512,
      "kv_cache_layout": "sharded",
      "prefer_fp16_math": true
    }
  }
}
```

carla: Interesting seq_switch difference — why 128 for A100/H100 and 512 for A10?

alice: On A100/H100 the large-tile kernels have excellent ramp-up for even small seqs because of huge tensor-core throughput and lower kernel launch overhead; the breakpoint where throughput path wins is much lower. On A10/L4/T4 the large-tile kernels waste shared mem and have worse occupancy at small seqs, so we push the switch later (to favor more conservative kernels until seq grows).

ben: How about KV cache behavior? Any surprises?

alice: Two main things: cached KV layout choice affects eviction and memcpy patterns. On A100 we do packed contiguous KV which benefits large tiles and single memcpy, on A10/T4 we shard KV per-head-block to avoid big memcpy spikes and to reduce per-kernel shared memory usage. That reduced jitter on the smaller devices.

perf-bot: autotune run complete: 1749501200 -> best presets found for a100_h100, a10_l4_t4 (see logs)

dmitri: Did you re-run PT-extract/tracing for kernel timings? Any perf regressions vs the previous runtime?

alice: Yes — we collected kernel-level traces via CUPTI and nvprof-style summaries. Biggest regression we saw earlier (before autotune) was a 15% p99 increase on A10 after a change in attention scheduling; autotuner recovered ~10% by swapping attention_impl and smaller tile sizes.

carla: Any actionable knobs we should expose in Console for customers?

alice: Suggest exposing 3 presets in Console per-device: 
- low-latency (seq_switch small, kv_layout sharded)
- balanced (autotuner default)
- cost-optimized (favor throughput kernels, higher batch aggregation)
And show a simple perf estimate delta vs hosted default.

ben: Can you share command lines to reproduce the run? I'll push to our perf CI.
alice: Sure — the driver script we used: 
```bash
./perf_runner.py \
  --model gpt-1.2B \
  --device $DEVICE \
  --seq_len 512 \
  --batch 4 \
  --preset presets/${DEVICE}.json \
  --trace kernelevents.cuplist
```
Also small helper to run seq-sweep: 
```bash
for s in 8 32 128 256 512 1024; do \
  DEVICE=a10 python perf_runner.py --model gpt-1.2B --device $DEVICE --seq_len $s --batch 4 --preset presets/a10.json; \
done
```

dmitri: Nice. One more ask: can we add a micro-benchmark for KV memcpy vs compute balance on L4/T4? I want a repeatable number for when to prefer sharded vs packed.

alice: Good idea — I'll add a small kv_bench that measures memcpy time per token and compute time per token across seqs and devices. Will post results in this thread.

carla: Thanks — very actionable. If we can expose the presets + perf estimates in Console, ops teams will love it. :thumbsup:

alice: Will follow up with a short doc and perf CSV later today.
